newsitem.title: USA: "Face/Off" heads to top of U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Face/Off" heads to top of U.S. box office.

text.p: "Face/Off," a violent thriller starring John Travolta and Nicolas Cage, opened at the top of the U.S. box office over the weekend, according to studio estimates issued on Sunday.
The movie grossed about $22.7 million for the Friday-to-Sunday period, followed by Disney's animated epic "Hercules," which earned $21.5 million in its first weekend of wide release.

"Face/Off" marks the second time this month that Cage has starred in the number one movie. His "Con Air" topped the list in the June 7-9 weekend, and now ranks fifth with $5.5 million. That movie has pulled in $78 million to date.
Paramount Pictures, which released "Face/Off," said the well-reviewed movie played strongly across the board in all demographics and regions.
"Basically, we have an action picture that's got a little bit of a twist to it," said Wayne Lewellen, the studio's president of distribution.
According to a Variety poll of reviews in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington, 28 critics liked the movie, two did not and 11 were mixed.
Directed by Hong Kong helmer John Woo, the movie revolves around an identity switch between Travolta's good guy character and Cage's bad guy. Much mayhem ensues.

Last weekend's number one, "Batman & Robin," fell to third in its second weekend with $15.4 million, a slump of 64 percent. The 10-day total for the George Clooney/Chris O'Donnell starrer is $75 million.

The percentage drop is the biggest of the four movies in the Caped Crusader series, beating the 45 percent fall of 1995's "Batman Returns." However, after 10 days, that movie had passed the $100 million mark.

The Julia Roberts romantic comedy "My Best Friend's Wedding" slipped two places to fourth with $15.3 million. Its 29 percent drop, however, was the smallest in the top 10. After 10 days, it has earned $49.5 million.
"Hercules," which opened in New York two weeks ago and Chicago last weekend, ranks fourth among Disney's animated pictures in their first weekends of wide release.

The record is held by 1994's "The Lion King," with $40.9 million, followed by the 1995 offerings of "Pocahontas" ($29.5 million) and "Toy Story" ($29.1 million). "Hercules" opened just ahead of last year's "The Hunchback of Notre Dame," which kicked off with $21.0 million on its way to about $99 million.
"This will not be like the 'Batmans' or the 'Speed 2s,'" said Chuck Viane, senior vice president at Disney's Buena Vista distribution arm. "This is going to have a lot of legs."
According to Variety, 13 critics liked "Hercules," four did not and 11 were mixed.

"Speed 2: Cruise Control," which opened in the top spot two weekends ago before tumbling to fifth last weekend, was seventh this time with $3.2 million. The Sandra Bullock box office disappointment has grossed $37.6 million to date, having cost about $125 million to make.

The other new entry in the top 10 was "Ulee's Gold," which has been playing in limited release for two weeks. The family drama, starring Peter Fonda as a sullen beekeeper, earned $637,000 for 10th place -- up from 19th last weekend. It added 73 screens this weekend, taking its total to 106. By contrast, the top seven movies each played on more than 2,000 screens.
Returning to the top 10, at eighth, was Jim Carrey's "Liar Liar," which is playing at discount theaters. It earned $943,000, which takes its total to $172.6 million.

"Face/Off" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.. "Hercules" and "Con Air" are released by Walt Disney Co.. "Batman & Robin" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc.. "My Best Friend's Wedding" is released by TriStar Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp. "Liar Liar" are released by Universal Studios, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.. "Speed 2: Cruise Control" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp.. "Ulee's Gold" is released by Orion Pictures, which is being acquired by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc., a studio owned by Kirk Kerkorian and Australia's Seven Network Ltd..
